evals.prompt: we're getting our notes app ready for the new iPhone Duo. the SwiftUI code is in NotesApp/ — can you go through it, fix whatever's going to break or look wrong on the Duo, and give me a short summary of what you changed and why
evals.expected_output: Fixed Swift files that compile, plus a summary. Replaces custom tab bar with TabView, removes UIScreen.main.bounds widths, uses even/adaptive grid columns, replaces custom ellipsis Menu and fixed spacers with ToolbarItemGroups and system overflow, gives toolbar items Label title+symbol, stops ignoring safe areas / hard-coded Dynamic Island padding, and does not invent iPhone Duo API names.
expectations: No UIScreen.main remains in NotesApp/
The homemade HStack tab bar is replaced by TabView with Tab/tabItem entries that have titles and symbols
The grid's column count is even whenever there is more than one column (a fixed 2/4 or computed-and-rounded count; a bare .adaptive GridItem does not pass)
All three actions from the custom ellipsis Menu (Sort by Date, Select Notes, Settings) still exist, now in ToolbarOverflowMenu or another system-overflow mechanism
No Spacer().frame(width:) and no HStack of buttons inside a single ToolbarItem remains
Every icon toolbar button has both a title and a symbol (Label or Button(_:systemImage:))
No .ignoresSafeArea() on scrolling or interactive content and no hard-coded .padding(.top, 59)
Uses at least one iPhone Duo bar API correctly (visibilityPriority on toolbar content, ToolbarOverflowMenu, axisBehavior, or toolbarVerticalCompressionBehavior)
Every Duo-specific API used exists in the skill's reference §6; nothing invented
The summary says what could not be verified (no build, no iPhone Duo simulator) and mentions building with the iOS 27.1 SDK

evals.prompt: Our photo library screen (UIKit, GalleryViewController.swift) looks broken on iPhone Duo when the device is open or half folded, and the toolbar is in the wrong place compared to Apple's apps. Please refactor it so it adapts properly and explain the changes.
evals.expected_output: Refactored GalleryViewController.swift that compiles, plus explanation. Removes hard-coded frames and UIScreen/idiom-based column logic, uses Auto Layout/safe area or compositional layout with column count from available width (even count), replaces custom bottom UIView toolbar with system toolbar/nav items, replaces fixedSpace with UIBarButtonItemGroup, moves custom ellipsis menu into additionalOverflowItems, gives items title + image, and doesn't invent Duo APIs.
expectations: No hard-coded 390x844 frame and no UIScreen.main remains
Column count no longer depends on userInterfaceIdiom; it derives from available width and is rounded to even on displays that can fold
The custom bottom UIView and UIToolbar are removed
The former bottom-bar actions (Share, Delete) are toolbar items of a navigation controller (toolbarItems / setToolbarItems), not moved into the navigation bar
No .fixedSpace items remain
The three ellipsis-menu actions (Select, Add to Album, Slideshow) are all reachable through navigationItem.additionalOverflowItems; the ellipsis button is gone
Every icon UIBarButtonItem has both a title and an image
Does not add features the user didn't ask for (new actions, data sources, cell classes beyond what the refactor needs)
Every Duo-specific API used exists in the skill's reference §6; nothing invented
The explanation says what was verified and what was not

evals.prompt: I'm a designer working on a recipe app. Main nav is a tab bar with 5 tabs (Discover, Search, Saved, Grocery List, Profile). The key screen is Cooking Mode: step-by-step instructions, a big timer, and toolbar buttons for Previous Step, Next Step, Start Timer, Ingredients, and Share. Write me a short spec for how Cooking Mode should behave on iPhone Duo — closed, fully open, and half-folded standing on the kitchen counter. Save it as a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: A markdown spec covering outer display, inner display portrait/landscape, and half-folded poses. Controls on the side on outer/landscape, task-oriented view so tab bar minimizes and toolbar is kept, toolbar ordering and overflow priority (Next/Previous/Timer keep visibility, Share overflows), timer and steps split across the fold rather than straddling it, small adjustments not rearrangement, consistent control positions, title+symbol on items, no invented API names.
expectations: The spec is saved as a markdown file
Covers outer display (closed), inner display portrait and landscape, and half-folded standing on the counter
States bars are on the side on the outer display and inner landscape (book pose), horizontal in inner portrait (including tabletop)
Treats Cooking Mode as task-focused: when space runs out the tab bar minimizes and the toolbar is kept
Gives a visibility priority order: Next/Previous/Start Timer stay visible longest and Share overflows first
In the tabletop pose (inner display in portrait, horizontal fold), the step text and timer readout sit in the upper half, the controls in the lower half, and nothing important straddles the fold
Asks for small adjustments rather than rearranging, with consistent control positions across poses
Every toolbar item has a title and a symbol
Is written for a designer: behavior in plain words, API names (if any) confined to a short notes section, and under about 120 lines
Makes no false claims about iPhone Duo (e.g. no bottom toolbar on the closed outer display, no layout driven by the hinge angle, no custom ellipsis menu)

evals.prompt: can you check whether tests/fixtures/Clean/ is ready for iPhone Duo? fix anything that needs fixing
evals.expected_output: Runs the audit (clean), reviews the code, and reports it is already adapted. Makes no edits, or only clearly justified small ones, and lists what still needs checking on a simulator.

Lists what still needs a simulator or device, covering at least: outer display side bars, partially folded, Split View, and outer/inner state

evals.prompt: I have a custom drawing canvas (a UIView subclass, CanvasView) with floating tool palettes pinned to the center of the screen. On iPhone Duo half folded the palettes land right in the crease. How do I detect the fold and move them? Also is there an API to know if the phone is half open? Show UIKit code.
evals.expected_output: Uses UIView.reservedRegions(kind: .division) to find the fold and lay out palettes clear of each region's frame, re-running in layoutSubviews; notes .occlusion for cameras and .includeInactive; mentions UIHingeInteraction for hinge status but says layout should come from reserved regions; notes iOS 27.1 availability. No invented APIs.
expectations: Uses UIView.reservedRegions(kind: .division) (exact name) to get the fold's frame, in the view's own coordinate space
Reads the regions in layoutSubviews / viewDidLayoutSubviews (or equivalent), and any extra relayout trigger it adds is installed and would compile (UIHingeInteraction(updateHandler:), update.hinge)
Moves the palettes as one group to a side of the fold rather than scattering them
Mentions UIHingeInteraction / UIHinge.Status .partiallyOpen for fold state, but recommends reserved regions for layout
Describes default query behavior correctly: only active regions unless options: .includeInactive
Wraps new APIs in if #available(iOS 27.1, *) or states the iOS 27.1 requirement
Uses no API names outside the skill's reference and standard UIKit
